auth_methods.quote: include authentication information using either of the following: Using key pair authentication Using OAuth Using a programmatic access token (PAT) Using workload identity federation
auth_methods.note: Key-pair JWT, OAuth, programmatic access tokens (bearer) and workload identity federation.

credential_access.quote: The trial continues for 30 days (from the sign-up date) or until you’ve depleted your free usage balance, whichever occurs first.
credential_access.note: No permanent free tier; self-serve 30-day/credit-limited trial, then paid account. Admin in the customer account also must create OAuth/key-pair users.

production_gate.quote: Using OAuth ¶ To use OAuth, follow these steps: Set up OAuth for authentication.
production_gate.note: OAuth is configured by each customer's account admin via a security integration; no Snowflake-side app review or partner step documented for building a connector.

api_type.note: SQL API and Snowflake REST APIs documented; drivers/connectors/CLI also exist, but REST is the HTTP API.

mcp_official.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open-source standard that lets AI agents securely interact with business applications and external data systems, such as databases and content repositories.
mcp_official.note: Page documents the Snowflake-managed MCP server (hosted in customer account).

main_blocker_type.quote: At the end of the trial, the account is suspended.
main_blocker_type.note: Account is required, trial expires, then paid; also account-admin setup. Reading as access (customer-admin setup) is plausible.
